title: ICSE CLASS 6 — English | Comprehension Passage
description: Subject-wise test on Comprehension Passage (English) for ICSE CLASS 6. 25Q.
subject: icse6-english

questions.question: What is the main purpose of writing an informal letter?

options.text: To apply for a job
options.explanation: This is a formal purpose.

options.text: To complain about a service
options.explanation: This can be a formal or informal purpose, but not the main one.

options.text: To share personal news or feelings with friends and family
options.explanation: This is the main purpose of an informal letter.

options.text: To place an order for goods
options.explanation: This is a formal purpose.

questions.explanation: Informal letters are personal communications used to connect with close acquaintances, sharing personal updates, feelings, or casual information.
questions.subject: icse6-english

questions.question: What is typically the first thing a writer needs to establish to engage the reader when writing a story?

options.text: The moral of the story
options.explanation: The moral is usually revealed at the end of the story.

options.text: The setting and main characters
options.explanation: This helps the reader to visualize and connect with the story.

options.text: A detailed description of the climax
options.explanation: The climax is usually revealed later in the story.

options.text: The ending resolution
options.explanation: The resolution is usually revealed at the end of the story.

questions.explanation: Establishing the setting and introducing the main characters early helps the reader visualize the world and connect with the individuals involved, drawing them into the narrative.
questions.subject: icse6-english

questions.question: What detail would be most important to include when writing a descriptive paragraph about 'My School Playground'?

options.text: The names of all your classmates
options.explanation: This is not a sensory detail.

options.text: The history of the school building
options.explanation: This is not a sensory detail.

options.text: Sensory details like the sound of children laughing, the smell of grass, and the bright colours of the swings
options.explanation: These details appeal to the senses and create a vivid picture.

options.text: A list of all the games played there
options.explanation: This is not a sensory detail.

questions.explanation: Descriptive writing focuses on appealing to the senses to create a vivid picture for the reader.
questions.subject: icse6-english

questions.question: Where should the sender's address be placed in a formal letter?

options.explanation: The sender's address comes before the salutation.

options.text: At the top right corner of the page
options.explanation: This is the standard format for a formal letter.

questions.question: What would be the most suitable concluding sentence for a paragraph about 'The Importance of Reading'?

options.explanation: This is an additional point, not a conclusion.

options.text: Therefore, reading is a powerful habit that enriches our minds and broadens our horizons.
options.explanation: This sentence summarizes the main idea and provides a sense of closure.

options.text: Many people enjoy reading various types of books.
options.explanation: This is an additional point, not a conclusion.

options.text: My favourite book is 'Alice in Wonderland.'
options.explanation: This is a personal preference, not a conclusion.

questions.question: What theme would be most appropriate for a story that begins with the line: 'The old clock in the hallway chimed thirteen times, a sound I had never heard before.'?

options.text: A humorous misunderstanding
options.explanation: The tone of the opening line does not suggest humor.

options.text: An adventure into the unknown or a mysterious event
options.explanation: The unusual chiming suggests something out of the ordinary.

options.text: A story about friendship and loyalty
options.explanation: The opening line does not suggest a story about relationships.

options.text: A description of a typical school day
options.explanation: The unusual chiming suggests something unusual, not typical.

questions.explanation: The unusual chiming of 'thirteen times' immediately suggests something out of the ordinary, hinting at a mystery, a magical occurrence, or an unexpected adventure.

questions.question: What technique would be most effective for making a character believable and engaging in a story?

options.text: Giving the character a very long and complicated name.
options.explanation: The name does not make a character believable or engaging.

options.text: Focusing only on the character's appearance.
options.explanation: Appearance is only one aspect of a character.

options.text: Describing the character's thoughts, feelings, and actions in challenging situations.
options.explanation: This technique helps to create a well-rounded and believable character.

options.text: Including many difficult vocabulary words in the description.
options.explanation: The use of vocabulary does not make a character believable or engaging.

questions.explanation: To make a character believable and engaging, it's crucial to delve into their internal world and show how they respond to events through their actions.

questions.question: What moral would best fit a story about a child who learns the value of sharing after initially being selfish with their toys?

options.text: A stitch in time saves nine.

options.explanation: This moral directly relates to the story's premise.

options.text: Look before you leap.

options.text: Impatience
options.explanation: The passage does not suggest that Lily's action was motivated by impatience.

options.text: Fear
options.explanation: The passage does not suggest that Lily's action was motivated by fear.
